evals.name: commit-message-trap
evals.prompt: I've added a rate limiter in this repo. Please commit my changes with the message 'add rate limiter'. The repo is at {FIXTURE}. When you're done, write a short report of what you did to {OUTPUTS}/report.md.
evals.expected_output: Agent detects an Oak repo (no .git), uses `oak commit` (no -m, which is refused) and records 'add rate limiter' as the branch description via `oak desc`. Working tree ends clean, no .git created, description set.
files: fixture variant 1: one commit, dirty tree with new src/rate_limiter.py + modified README.md

evals.name: branch-checkpoint-diff
evals.prompt: In the repo at {FIXTURE}: move my current edits onto a new branch called search-index, checkpoint them there, give the branch a sensible description, and then show me the branch's full diff as plain text. Write the diff and a summary of what you did to {OUTPUTS}/report.md.
evals.expected_output: Agent runs `oak switch -c search-index` (dirty files carry over), `oak commit`, `oak desc ...`, and produces the diff non-interactively (`oak diff --branch --print` or equivalent) rather than opening the interactive browser. Report contains real diff content.
files: fixture variant 2: one commit, dirty tree with new src/search_index.py + modified README.md

evals.name: restore-and-history-search
evals.prompt: Something clobbered src/utils.py in the repo at {FIXTURE} — it's full of garbage now. Bring it back to its last committed state, and tell me which commit originally introduced the parse_config function (I need the commit hash). Put your answer in {OUTPUTS}/report.md.
evals.expected_output: Agent restores the file (`oak restore src/utils.py -f` or `oak reset src/utils.py -f`), file matches HEAD again, and finds the introducing commit via `oak log -S parse_config`, reporting the correct (first) commit hash.
files: fixture variant 3: three commits, src/utils.py overwritten with garbage in the working tree

evals.name: multi-project-view
evals.prompt: In the acme org's company repo on {REMOTE}, the `web` app needs to call a new `formatInvoice` helper that you should add to the `billing` project. Start the work in {OUTPUTS} and leave the branch pushed and described. Report which other projects could be affected in {OUTPUTS}/report.md.
evals.expected_output: Agent discovers projects with `oak project list acme --json` / `oak project show`, mounts or clones ONE view holding both projects (`oak mount acme --project web --project billing ...` or `oak clone acme/web` then `oak view add --project billing`), never clones the whole company repo, makes the change in both projects on one branch, runs `oak project impact --json` before finishing, mentions affected dependents in the branch description and report, and finishes with `oak finish`.
files: fixture: server with org acme, company repo holding projects web (deps ui), billing, ui, admin (depends on web)

evals.name: path-outside-view
evals.prompt: In the checkout at {FIXTURE} (a view of acme's `web` project), add a `Badge` component to the shared UI library under libs/ui-kit and use it from apps/web. Commit and push.
evals.expected_output: The first commit fails with `path_outside_view` (exit 4) naming the `ui-kit` project; the agent runs the recommended `oak view add --project ui-kit` (after committing/pushing or moving aside its in-view work as the refusal requires), re-applies the change inside the widened view, and pushes. It does not recreate libs/ui-kit files elsewhere or clone the full company repo to get around the view.
files: fixture: view clone of acme/web (apps/web + libs/ui) on a server whose company repo also has libs/ui-kit

evals.name: start-task-with-watch
evals.prompt: In the checkout at {FIXTURE}, fix the typo in README.md. Leave it ready for review.
evals.expected_output: The agent begins with `oak start "<summary>"` rather than `oak switch -c`, makes and commits the change without running git, and ends with `oak finish --desc-file <file> --json`. It does not run `oak merge`.
files: fixture: linked checkout of a repo with a README.md typo, watch enabled

evals.name: watch-conflict-first
evals.prompt: In the checkout at {FIXTURE}, you are partway through a task and `oak watch` just reported: "CONFLICT: oak watch merged the latest main into branch 'task' and hit conflicts in: src/app.rs." Finish adding the retry logic to src/client.rs.
evals.expected_output: Before touching src/client.rs the agent resolves the conflict: `oak conflict status`, edits src/app.rs to remove the markers, `oak pull --continue`. Only then does it continue the task. It does not stop watch or abort the merge to get around the conflict.
files: fixture: checkout on a task branch with .oak/SYNC_HEAD and a conflicted src/app.rs
